_what_this_is: The human rulings register. Every design decision the USER made, in the user's own words, with the date and the session it was said in. A ruling is not a feature and not a plan - it is a thing the user settled that the build is not free to re-derive. Declining a ruling is allowed; forgetting one is not.
_why_it_exists: Ruling RL-019 was given on 2026-08-17 after the user found that a design they had settled on 2026-08-03 was only 2/22 built. The pattern behind it: rulings were recorded as prose inside whichever document was open at the time, or not at all, so nothing could enumerate them and nothing could measure whether the running system honoured them. Section 3a of the goal document is the counter-example that worked - the ruling was written verbatim the moment it was given.
_how_status_is_decided: It is NOT decided here. No row carries a status field on purpose. Each row names a probe; statuswall.ruling_conformance runs it and the board renders what it measured. A ruling with probe:null renders NOT MEASURED, never green (Rule 8). Typing a status into this file would be exactly the fiction the board exists to prevent.
_source_note: Rows sourced 'transcript' were recovered on 2026-08-17 from ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl by reading every user message in the project's history. Verbatim text is reproduced as typed, including typos - it is the user's wording, not a cleaned-up paraphrase, because a paraphrase is how the meaning drifts.

Chosen in interview: the model drives paper trading immediately - RL-005 makes paper the place for unrestricted experiment and no capital is at risk - while the promotion gate governs any future real-money step. rulings.verbatim: [interview answer] New entries only; check the alias file every poll and load only when the id changed
rulings.clarified_as: When a new champion registers while a bot is running, the bot picks it up WITHOUT a restart, and the swap applies to NEW ENTRIES ONLY: a position already open keeps the brains that opened it until it closes. The bot checks the champion alias on every poll - a stat of a small file - and loads a model only when the version id actually changed.
rulings.means: A trade whose P&L is split across two models is attributable to neither, which is the same failure as crediting one P&L to 36 features. Every fill already carries its brains by name, and this keeps that record true. A bot that only picks up a champion at process start is a bot that never uses most of what the retrainer fits.

rulings.verbatim: [interview answer] A row in a segment slice covers that segment's three brains
rulings.clarified_as: Per-brain coverage is counted by attributing a row to the brains of the segment slice it sits in: a row in spot-bot counts for spot-bot/BULL, spot-bot/BEAR and spot-bot/PROFIT-TAIL together. A row in a shared or cross-cutting slice attributes to no brain, because a capability built once is not thereby delivered to four bots.
rulings.means: The arithmetic had a denominator of twelve brains and a numerator that counted slice keys, and a slice key can never equal a brain name - so all nine per-brain rulings read 0/12 and always would have, including RL-026 and RL-030. A fraction that can only be zero is not a measurement. Attribution follows how the bots are actually built: a capability lands in a segment bot and its three brains receive it at once. A shared slice still counting for all four is the very failure the scope arithmetic exists to catch.

rulings.verbatim: [interview answer] Repartition: one file per hour per venue
rulings.clarified_as: A whole-universe dataset - funding and the option chain, where every consumer wants all symbols for a window rather than one symbol - is partitioned by availability hour and compacted to ONE PART PER VENUE within that hour, not one per symbol. The symbol moves into the file body, because the path no longer carries it. Datasets that are read per-symbol, bars and book, keep their symbol layout.
rulings.means: Per-symbol parts of a poll-wide dataset are too small to be worth opening: one sealed funding hour held 1,892 fragments for 26,015 rows and 16.2 MiB - 13.8 rows per file - at 29 ms each, so the whole 850 MB dataset cost 30.6 minutes to read and grew by ~1,021 files an hour. That is what froze the status wall for two days. Column pushdown filters rows; it cannot prune files.

rulings.verbatim: [interview answer] Probes read a bounded window, not the whole archive
rulings.clarified_as: The status wall's expensive probes are bounded to the newest hours of a dataset rather than materialising the whole archive, and each tile STATES THE WINDOW IT MEASURED. A number whose scope is on its face is a measurement; the same number presented as covering everything is an assertion.
rulings.means: The wall could not finish a pass at all: it last completed 2026-08-17 13:38 and its probe cache had never been created, because the five expensive probes materialise the whole bars dataset - 208,880 fragments - reaching 7 GB before the kernel killed them. A board that never returns reports nothing, which is worse than a board reporting a bounded number honestly. Hour partitioning is what makes the bound cheap, and bars keeps its per-symbol layout because the bots read it that way.

rulings.verbatim: [interview answer] Convert bars, and widen the wall window back out
rulings.clarified_as: Bars is converted to the hour-only layout like funding and the option chain, and once it is, the wall's expensive probes stop needing a tight window: the tiles report over a long window, or the whole record, because the read is cheap rather than because the scope was narrowed.
rulings.means: The premise of keeping a symbol partition was that some reader prunes by it. Nothing does: `ClockGatedReader` applies `symbols` to the already-materialised frame, and the only pushdown filters in the store are on availability time and the hour. So the symbol level cost bars 208,880 fragments and pruned for nobody. A window that exists because the data is badly laid out is a narrowed claim paying for an avoidable cost; once the layout is fixed the honest answer is also the cheap one.

rulings.verbatim: I need you to create a edit option on top of the 2 spot and future segment bots of the total papper capital from the total portfolio that the 2 segment bots can use and the min and max capital per trade / [interview answers] A config file the bots re-read live; Shared pool with a per-bot cap; Margin posted
rulings.clarified_as: One editable JSON file, `~/capture/segment/capital.json`, is the single declaration of how much paper capital the perp and spot bots may use. It holds the portfolio total, the fraction of it either single bot may hold at once, and the minimum and maximum MARGIN per trade. Both bots re-read it live on the poll after its mtime changes - no restart - the same way the model alias file is reloaded under RL-030.
rulings.means: OVERTURNS the line in `src/segment/capital_accounting.py` that reads *'It is a measurement base, not a limit - the risk gate owns limits and does not read it.'* The declared capital becomes a BUDGET that is actually spent and can actually be exhausted, and the gate now reads it. Three consequences that are not optional. First, the pool is SHARED across two independent OS processes, so headroom must be reserved under a real lock on the pool file, not computed from each bot's own view - two bots reading a stale balance and both opening is how a shared pool silently overshoots. Second, capital per trade means MARGIN POSTED, so with leverage the position notional is a multiple of it and every P&L, drawdown and excursion figure is denominated on the notional while the pool is debited the margin; mixing the two is the unit error this whole ruling exists to prevent. Third, a missing or malformed file must STOP the bots opening rather than fall back to a default - capital silently chosen by a default is capital chosen by nobody.

rulings.verbatim: And the spot and futures have leverage option s like 5x or 10x or 20x / [interview answer] Both bots, chosen per trade
rulings.clarified_as: Both the perp bot and the spot bot size positions with leverage, and the multiple is chosen per trade rather than fixed per bot, under a ceiling declared per segment in `capital.json`. Warned at the time that this is the most demanding of the four options and needs a borrow-cost model, per-trade sizing and a liquidation-distance check before it is safe; the user chose it with that stated.
rulings.means: Leverage does not exist anywhere in the codebase today - zero references to leverage, margin, liquidation or isolated/cross - so this is new construction, not a setting to expose. Three prerequisites are part of this ruling and may not be deferred, because each one is a way for leverage to report a profit that is not real. (1) SPOT BORROW COST: leveraged spot is borrowed money, and not charging interest on it makes the spot bot's returns a free loan that inflates every figure it publishes. (2) LIQUIDATION DISTANCE: at L times leverage an isolated position liquidates on roughly a 1/L adverse move, so a hard stop wider than that is a stop that can never fire - the position dies first. The gate must refuse, or reduce leverage until the stop fits, and name which it did. (3) THE CHOOSING RULE MUST BE DECLARED AND JOURNALLED: the default is volatility-targeted, leverage = target risk over the instrument's realised volatility, clamped to the declared ceiling - NOT confidence-scaled, because the perp and spot brains currently journal `calibrated=False` and scaling leverage by an uncalibrated confidence compounds the miscalibration exactly where it costs most. The rule is named in the config file so it can be changed without a code change.

rulings.verbatim: and a data coloum of peak profit and loss that the trade reach after placed
rulings.clarified_as: Every trade records the best and the worst it ever got while it was open - maximum favourable excursion and maximum adverse excursion - journalled on CLOSE and shown as columns beside the realised P&L.
rulings.means: Measured 2026-08-19: `peak_favourable` is declared on `OpenPosition` and copied on ratchet but NEVER ASSIGNED anywhere in the codebase, so it has been `None` for every position that has ever existed, and there is no adverse counterpart at all. A field that looks built and is not is worse than an absent one. Both excursions are tracked on every poll, as a fraction of entry AND in USDT on the position notional, and both are journalled on CLOSE. They must be labelled SAMPLED: the engine polls every six seconds and cannot see the true extreme between polls, so the journalled figure is a lower bound on the real excursion and the sample count is recorded beside it. This is what makes the exit policy auditable - a trade that reached +0.9% before closing at -0.2% is a profit tail that let go, and without these two columns that failure is invisible.

rulings.verbatim: do all 3
rulings.clarified_as: All three of the offered steps: gate the champion alias assignment through a real promotion decision, never promote a model that does not beat the incumbent on the same out-of-fold measure, and only then decide what to do with the model perp is currently running.
rulings.means: MEASURED 2026-08-19: the champion alias is assigned UNCONDITIONALLY by `learn.train_segment_model` line 247. The only check is a binomial test against the majority class; `models.model_registry.assign_alias` reads the incumbent solely to record it as `previous_version_id` and never compares. So the champion is whatever trained LAST, not what is best, and a retrain that produces a worse model silently replaces a better one. The promotion machinery already exists - `validation.promotion_gate`, `validation.promotion_pipeline`, `models.champion_challenger` - and outside their own files the only importer is a statuswall PROBE. Built, tested, and wired to nothing that promotes anything: the exact trap CLAUDE.md names with `tail_specs()`. What it cost, the same day: perp's champion moved 976ee2399a5c -> 9fa37695dae0 at 15:34 with accuracy 0.5486 both times, but the base rate rose from 0.5316 to 0.5363, so the EDGE fell from 1.70 to 1.23 percentage points on 42% fewer out-of-fold rows. The outgoing model had opened 3,352 positions; the incoming one proposed 10 times in 600 polls and selected none. NOTE the check that does NOT discriminate here: effective sample fraction was 0.0022 for the outgoing model and 0.0038 for the incoming one, so a floor on it would have blocked the BETTER model too. Any threshold on effective sample is a separate decision with the power to stop all promotion, and is the user's to set rather than one to invent inside a gate.

_how_scope_works: Every ruling binds at a level, and the level decides the denominator the reconciliation counts against: per-segment needs a row in all four segment slices, per-brain in all twelve brains, shared and system need one row anywhere. Assigned once is not resolved four times - that is how a cross-cutting capability reads as done while three of four bots never received it. Default assignment (spec 2026-08-17 §5): decides about a symbol or market -> per-segment; about a brain's own learning, beliefs or competence -> per-brain; about capture, store, cost, validation, registry, tail cap or governance -> shared; whole-account objective -> system.
